function_analysis: Unchanged: lower mean wall shear at cruising speed (viscous length ~5-8 um), keep fouling off or releasable without biocides, survive 3-5 years (abrasion by fenders and cleaning is the dominant killer of soft foul-release coatings), no large consumption, hull-scale application. The graded-stiffness family mainly serves fouling release and damage tolerance; any direct drag effect must come from dissipative interaction with near-wall pressure and shear fluctuations and is small at ship Reynolds numbers.

requirements.name: low_friction_drag
requirements.criterion: Reduces the mean wall shear stress / frictional resistance at cruising speed versus a clean, standard foul-release hull coating.

requirements.name: non_toxic_antifouling
requirements.criterion: Prevents fouling settlement or makes it release easily without releasing biocides, heavy metals or other toxic substances into the sea.

requirements.name: multi_year_seawater_durability
requirements.criterion: Keeps its function and adhesion for at least 3-5 years in seawater (hydrolysis, abrasion, UV at the waterline, cleaning).

requirements.name: low_consumption_operation
requirements.criterion: Needs no continuous supply of material or energy that is large compared with the fuel it saves, and no frequent reapplication.

requirements.name: hull_scale_applicability
requirements.criterion: Can be applied to large steel hull areas with dry-dock methods at a cost comparable to premium hull coatings.

mechanism_classes_considered: graded_stiffness (dissipative soft-over-stiff layers; hard armour over soft foundation)
phase_change (vapour layers, degassing, melting) - checked for energy balance
trapped_gas_or_liquid (gas layers fed by gas generation)
analogues_considered: Grease ice and frazil slush on the polar ocean: a soft, highly dissipative layer over consolidated ice that damps waves over a broad band
Mud banks off the Kerala coast damping waves by viscous dissipation in fluid mud
Desert pavement: a mosaic of hard, interlocking clasts resting on soft, fine-grained vesicular soil
Cyanobacterial gas vesicles and oxygen bubbles from phototrophic biofilms
Leidenfrost vapour layers on hot spheres (known drag reduction in lab)

candidates.title: Grease-ice broadband dissipative gel skin
candidates.summary: A 3 mm coating copying the vertical structure of young sea ice: a very lossy, soft silicone-gel top (G ~ 60 kPa, tan delta ~ 1, like grease ice/frazil slush) grading into a stiffer, low-loss base (like consolidated ice). Instead of tuning a resonance (dolphin-skin approach) it absorbs near-wall pressure fluctuations over a broad band, which makes the effect less speed-sensitive, and the soft top keeps a low fouling-release stress.

back_of_envelope.quantity: Reduction of mean wall shear at 7 m/s versus a clean standard silicone foul-release coating
back_of_envelope.formula: Energy absorbed by the wall per unit area ~ pi * tan_delta * p'^2 * t / G per cycle, with p'_rms ~ 2.5 tau = 45 Pa: E ~ 3.14*1*2025*3e-3/6e4 = 3.2e-4 J/m2 per cycle, times f ~ 300 Hz = 0.1 W/m2, compared with the turbulent production near the wall tau*U ~ 18*7 = 126 W/m2 -> a 0.08% share; even if the absorbed energy were taken entirely from the streak regeneration cycle with a leverage of ~10, DR ~ 0.8%; take 0.5%

candidates.main_risk: The dissipated power is three orders below the near-wall turbulence production, so the drag effect is likely unmeasurable, and a very soft lossy gel wears quickly.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: compliant coatings (Kramer, Choi) and the dolphin-skin elite, which rely on tuned resonance. New: broadband damping design taken from sea-ice wave attenuation (high-loss soft top, graded to a stiff base) - but my estimate shows the energy argument limits the drag effect to well below 1%.
candidates.baseline: Clean, standard silicone foul-release hull coating (~0.3 mm, E ~ 1 MPa) at 7 m/s
candidates.inspiration_source: Grease ice and frazil slush over consolidated sea ice, which damp ocean waves by viscous dissipation
candidates.physical_mechanism: Near-wall pressure and shear fluctuations deform a soft, lossy top layer; the loss modulus converts part of their energy into heat. The stiffness grading (soft/lossy top, stiff base) confines deformation near the surface and keeps the layer stable. Steady proxy model: 1D quasi-static deformation u(z) of the graded layer under a surface pressure/shear amplitude, from which the stored energy and, with tan_delta, the dissipated power per cycle follow; fouling release follows from surface compliance.

parameters.name: coating_thickness
parameters.justification: Thickness of the dissipative zone; young sea-ice slush layers are thicker, a hull coating is limited to a few mm.

parameters.name: surface_shear_modulus
parameters.justification: Soft gel top, kept >= 5e4 Pa for hydroelastic stability at 7 m/s.

parameters.name: base_shear_modulus
parameters.justification: Stiff, low-loss base like consolidated ice.

parameters.name: loss_tangent
parameters.justification: Highly dissipative gels reach tan delta ~ 1.

parameters.name: pressure_fluctuation_rms
parameters.justification: p'_rms ~ 2-3 tau_w in turbulent boundary layers.

candidates.infeasibility_reason: A phase-change drag layer on a hull needs either a vapour film (film boiling needs ~1e5 W/m2, i.e. ~1 GW for 1e4 m2, about 100x the ship's propulsion power, violating the energy balance of the request) or spontaneous degassing, which cannot occur because hydrostatic pressure keeps seawater under-saturated at hull depth; microbial gas production from seawater organics is 3-4 orders of magnitude too slow to feed even a thin gas layer.

candidates.title: Desert-pavement armoured compliant coating
candidates.summary: A mosaic of hard, flush, 3 mm ceramic-filled epoxy tiles (gap 50 um) floating on a 1.5 mm soft silicone foundation, copying desert pavement where interlocking hard clasts rest on soft vesicular soil. The hard tiles take fender, cleaning and abrasion loads that destroy soft foul-release coatings, while the soft foundation lets tiles rock individually, so a barnacle spanning several tiles is peeled off at a low load; the flush mosaic stays hydraulically smooth.

back_of_envelope.quantity: Change of mean wall shear at 7 m/s versus a clean standard silicone foul-release coating
back_of_envelope.formula: Tile gaps of 50 um, width w+ = 50e-6*0.13/1.05e-6 ~ 6 and depth-filled to 10 um: gap roughness k+ ~ 1-2 < 5, hydraulically smooth; tile edge misalignment 5 um -> k+ ~ 0.6. Friction change vs smooth FR ~ 0 +/- 0.5%. The benefit is durability, which keeps the hull smooth longer; clean-vs-clean drag gain ~0%.

candidates.main_risk: Hard tile surfaces give barnacles a strong bond; if tiles do not rock enough under a barnacle base (tile larger than barnacle), fouling release is worse than on soft silicone.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: soft silicone foul-release coatings (fragile) and hard ceramic-epoxy coatings (tough but poor release). New: hard-over-soft mosaic from desert pavement that separates the abrasion-bearing surface from the release-enabling compliance; not a textbook bionic surface.
candidates.baseline: Clean, standard silicone foul-release hull coating (~0.3 mm, E ~ 1 MPa) at 7 m/s
candidates.inspiration_source: Desert pavement: interlocking hard clasts on a soft, fine-grained vesicular soil layer
candidates.physical_mechanism: Hard tiles on an elastic Winkler-like foundation: a local load on a tile (fender, barnacle pull) is spread by the stiff tile and carried by the soft foundation; under a barnacle whose base spans tile edges, differential tile rotation concentrates peel at the base edge and lowers the release force. Wall shear stays that of a smooth wall because the tiles are flush. Steady model: 1D beam (tile) on elastic foundation under a point or distributed pull, or the sublayer shear over a smooth wall with an equivalent roughness correction.

parameters.name: tile_size
parameters.justification: Clast-like tiles; smaller than a mature barnacle base (5-15 mm) so a barnacle spans several tiles.

parameters.name: gap_width
parameters.justification: Gap between tiles, filled flush with soft silicone.
